tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
To add complex numbers, we just add the real parts and add the imaginary parts separately. For example,

$$
\begin{aligned}(3+5\text{i})+(2-3\text{i}) & =(3+5\text{i})+(2-3\text{i}) \\  & =(3+2)+(5+(-\,3))\text{i} \\  & =(3+2)+(5-3)\text{i} \\  & =5+2\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

In general, we write

$$
(a + b\textrm{i}) + (c + d\textrm{i}) = (a + c) + (b + d)\textrm{i}.
$$

Subtracting complex numbers works in the same way: we just subtract the real parts and subtract the imaginary parts separately. For example,

$$
\begin{aligned}(3+5\text{i})-(2-3\text{i}) & =(3+5\text{i})-(2-3\text{i}) \\  & =(3-2)+(5-(-\,3))\text{i} \\  & =(3-2)+(5+3)\text{i} \\  & =1+8\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

In general, we write

$$
(a + b\textrm{i}) - (c + d\textrm{i}) = (a - c) + (b - d)\textrm{i}.
$$
